records.text: Write a Python class that implements a least-recently-used cache with a fixed capacity. The class should expose get(key) and put(key, value) methods, both running in constant amortized time. Internally keep a dictionary from keys to nodes plus a doubly linked list that tracks recency, moving a node to the front on every access and evicting the tail node when the capacity is exceeded. Add a docstring, type hints, and a short example that inserts three keys, reads one of them back, and shows which key is evicted next.

Given a table of orders with columns customer_id, order_date, and total_cents, write a SQL query that returns each customer's third most recent order. Use a window function that partitions by customer, orders by order_date descending, and filters on the row number rather than on a self join. Handle customers with fewer than three orders by excluding them, and explain why the filter has to sit in an outer query or in a common table expression instead of the WHERE clause of the same SELECT that computes the row number.

Explain how Rust's borrow checker treats a function that takes a mutable slice of a vector and also needs to read the vector's length. Write a function that increments every element of the slice by one, then another that returns the index of the first negative value. Point out where a second mutable borrow would be rejected at compile time, how to restructure the code with split_at_mut, and why returning an index instead of a reference sidesteps the lifetime problem.

Write a JavaScript function that fetches a JSON document with exponential backoff, retrying up to five times on network errors and on server responses in the 500 range. Each delay should double starting from a quarter second, and the function should reject with the last error once the budget is exhausted. Use async and await, an AbortController for cancellation, and avoid retrying on client errors in the 400 range. Finish with a small usage example that logs the parsed field named items.

Show a shell pipeline that finds every Python file under a source directory, skips virtual environments and caches, and runs a formatter over the files in batches. Use find with a null byte separator so that spaces in file names cannot split an argument, pipe the list through xargs with a maximum argument count, and print a summary line at the end. Explain why the naive version that pipes find output into a while read loop can drop the exit status of the formatter and how to preserve it with the pipefail option.

Implement a singly linked list in C with push, pop, and reverse operations. Define the node struct with an integer value and a next pointer, allocate nodes with malloc, and free them in a destroy function that walks the chain. The reverse function should relink the pointers iteratively without allocating new nodes. Discuss the three-pointer technique, what happens on an empty list, and why a recursive reverse risks a stack overflow for long lists. Include a main function that builds a list of five values and prints it forwards.

Compute the derivative of f of x equals the natural logarithm of one plus x squared, raised to the third power. State the chain rule step by step: first differentiate the outer cube, then the logarithm, then the inner polynomial, and multiply the three factors. Simplify the result into a single fraction, identify the domain where the expression is differentiable, and evaluate the derivative at x equal to one. Then find the second derivative at the same point and comment on the sign of the first derivative on either side of zero.

A committee of four people must be chosen from a group of seven women and five men. Count the number of committees that contain exactly two women, and then count the committees that contain at least one man. Explain why the second count is easier to obtain by subtracting the all-women committees from the total. Then compute the probability that a uniformly random four-person committee contains exactly two women, and verify that the probabilities of zero, one, two, three, and four women sum to one.

Let A be a real three by three matrix whose rows are linearly independent. Show that the columns are also linearly independent, and explain the role of the determinant in that argument. Suppose one row is replaced by the sum of the other two rows: describe how the rank and the determinant change, and whether the column space shrinks. Finish by stating the dimension theorem for linear maps between finite dimensional spaces and applying it to the map defined by A acting on three dimensional vectors.

A medical test detects a disease in ninety-nine percent of infected people and wrongly flags one percent of healthy people. The disease affects one person in ten thousand. Compute the probability that a person who tests positive actually has the disease, writing out Bayes' rule, the prior, the likelihood, and the evidence term. Then recompute the same probability when the prevalence rises to one percent, and explain in plain language why the posterior changes so sharply with prevalence even though the test itself did not change.

Determine whether the series whose terms are n factorial divided by n to the power n converges. Apply the ratio test, simplify the ratio into a product that tends to one over e, and conclude. Then compare with the series of one over n squared and explain why one converges while the harmonic series diverges. State the integral test and use it to justify the convergence of the p-series for p strictly greater than one, and finally bound the tail of the p-series with an integral.

Consider minimizing the quadratic function given by one half x transpose A x minus b transpose x, where A is symmetric positive definite. Derive the gradient descent update with step size alpha, determine the largest step size that keeps the iteration stable in terms of the largest eigenvalue of A, and identify the condition number that governs the convergence rate. Then write the update for a two by two diagonal A with entries four and one, choose a step size, and explain why the slow direction dominates the error.

Describe the formation of the Andes mountain range. Explain how the subduction of an oceanic plate beneath the South American plate produces crustal thickening, volcanism, and a high plateau, and why the range is narrow in some latitudes and broad in others. Mention the role of the Nazca plate, the age of the descending lithosphere, and the sediment supply from the Amazon basin to the trench. Then contrast this ocean-continent setting with the collision of two continental plates that built the Himalayas.

Explain how movable type printing changed the circulation of texts in fifteenth century Europe. Cover the earlier use of woodblock printing, the innovation of reusable metal casts and oil-based ink, and the economics of setting a page. Describe how the reduced cost per copy shifted the scale of publishing from scribal workshops to commercial presses, and how the resulting abundance of pamphlets interacted with religious controversy and with the growth of vernacular literacy. Note one important limit on the speed of that change.

Summarize the periodic trends in electronegativity across a row and down a group of the periodic table. Explain the underlying causes in terms of effective nuclear charge and atomic radius, and connect the trend to the polarity of bonds and to the acidity of binary hydrogen compounds. Give two examples that follow the trend and one apparent exception, and explain the exception with atomic size and shielding rather than with a single number on a scale. Then explain why the noble gases are usually left out of the trend entirely, and why the scale is defined by a convention rather than measured directly.

Explain how stars on the main sequence produce energy through hydrogen fusion. Describe the proton-proton chain and the carbon-nitrogen-oxygen cycle, and say which dominates at which temperature. Discuss why the luminosity of a main sequence star scales steeply with its mass, how the star remains in hydrostatic equilibrium, and what happens to the core once hydrogen is exhausted. Then explain how observations of a cluster's turnoff point yield its age.

Describe the role of mitochondria in cellular energy metabolism. Explain how the electron transport chain builds a proton gradient across the inner membrane, how ATP synthase converts that gradient into chemical energy, and why oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Contrast the yield of ATP from glycolysis alone with the yield from complete oxidation, and mention the endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria and the evidence from their own genome.

Explain the principle of comparative advantage and how it predicts gains from trade between two countries even when one is more productive in every industry. State the assumptions about factor mobility, transport costs, and constant returns, then describe how a tariff affects consumer prices, producer surplus, and total welfare. Distinguish the static welfare loss from the dynamic effects on specialization, and give one reason why the empirical estimates of the losses are often small relative to the political attention the policy receives.

The lighthouse keeper had counted the same nine ships that week, so the tenth one, arriving without lights in the fog, made him set down his tea and reach for the logbook. He wrote the time, the bearing, and the fact that the vessel did not answer the signal lamp. Outside, the sea threw itself against the rocks in long grey ropes, and the gull that lived on the north railing refused to move. He climbed the stairs twice to be sure of what he had seen, and both times the shape was still there, closer, patient, running dark.

At the train station they stood on opposite sides of a pillar because neither wanted to be the first to speak. The departure board clicked through its permutations above them, and a woman with a cello case argued quietly with a porter. You could have called, he said at last, and she said she had, twice, and that the second time she had let it ring until the recorded voice asked her to leave a message and she had left one. The train for the coast was announced. He picked up her bag before she could, and they walked together toward the platform.

By the time the market opened, the street had already been awake for hours. Men unloaded crates of oranges still cold from the night, a woman arranged bundles of parsley into a green wall, and somewhere behind the stalls a radio played a song about a river. Steam rose from the tea stall and hung in the cold air, and the first customers drifted in with their collars up, testing the peaches with their thumbs. The light came slowly, sliding down the rooftops, until the whole street was gold and everyone began to talk at once.

The generation ship had been travelling for four hundred years when the child asked what a sky was. The teacher showed her the archive footage again, and the children watched the clouds move and argued about whether the water in the recording could really fall from above. In the corridor outside, the hydroponics fans turned with their endless patience, and the hull carried its low note through the floor plates. She decided that a sky must be something like the ceiling of the atrium, only farther, and she wrote that down in her notebook before the bell.

It had been raining since the funeral, which the detective took as a personal insult. He stood under the awning of the closed pharmacy and watched the house across the street, where a single lamp burned behind a curtain that had not moved in an hour. The case was three days old and already bent out of shape: a stolen car that nobody reported, a key that fit no lock in the building, and a witness who kept changing the colour of the coat. He lit a cigarette, put it out, and crossed the road.

Every summer we went back to the river, and every summer my grandmother insisted that the water was colder than the year before. She would sit on the flat stone with her skirt tucked under her and tell me which rocks to avoid, though I never once saw her swim. The current carried leaves past in a slow procession, and the bridge upstream hummed whenever a truck crossed it. Years later I understood that she had been keeping watch, the way you keep watch over something you are not ready to give up.
